market_summary:
Markets are reeling from a one-day AI-regulation panic: the Nasdaq fell ~5.5-6.4% and the Dow lost 1,833 points on Nov 5 after Democratic midterm gains raised fears of tighter AI oversight, hammering semis (sector index -12%) and mega-cap tech (NVDA -8.9% to -12%, TSLA -13.8%, META/GOOGL down double digits over the month). Apple and Amazon bucked the selloff, rising 3-4% intraday, with Apple also pricing a well-oversubscribed $7.5B bond deal, suggesting investors are rotating toward "safer" megacaps with less AI-capex/regulatory exposure. In Singapore, the three banks reported mixed Q3 results (DBS and OCBC beat estimates, UOB missed) but all fell with the global risk-off tape; SGX stocks with less US-tech linkage (STI, REITs, banks) sold off less violently than the Nasdaq-heavy names. Overall this looks like a sharp, headline-driven de-risking event rather than a fundamental shift, so near-term volatility should stay elevated into NVDA's Nov 17 earnings.</market_summary>
